caveats: Single-target dispatch — no DOM tree, so no capture/bubble/propagation (`stopPropagation` is a no-op; `stopImmediatePropagation` halts the remaining listeners)

`removeEventListener` matches by closure identity, so the listener must be a named binding (an inline arrow re-emitted at the remove site won't match); a 0-argument listener is rejected (the event parameter is required)
`{ once }` honored; `capture`/`passive`/`signal` options accepted but ignored (`signal` cancellation arrives with `AbortController`)
No `class X extends EventTarget` (built-in `extends` targets are rejected)
notes: A bare `Map<string, listener-list>` reusing EventEmitter's registry + snapshot dispatch; `dispatchEvent` reads `event.type`, invokes each listener with the event object, and returns `!defaultPrevented` ([TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00235](../adr/ADR-00235.md))

caveats: V1 surface is `type`, `defaultPrevented`, `cancelable`, and `CustomEvent.detail` (type inferred from the value); the fuller WHATWG properties (`target`/`currentTarget`/`bubbles`/`composed`/`timeStamp`/`eventPhase`/`isTrusted`) are absent

`bubbles` in the `new Event(type, { … })` init is accepted but ignored (single-target dispatch); `cancelable` **is** honored — `preventDefault()` sets `defaultPrevented` only on a cancelable event, a no-op otherwise ([ADR-00587](../adr/ADR-00587.md))
`stopPropagation()` is a no-op (single-target dispatch, no capture/bubble tree)
notes: Plain fixed-shape objects tagged `IsEvent`; construction + field reads + `preventDefault`/`stop*` work standalone. Dispatching them is `EventTarget` (next row) — [TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00234](../adr/ADR-00234.md)

caveats: A bare `signal.aborted` read reflects a `timeout` only after some await loop has checked it (no background latching); `signal` is wired into `fetch` but not `setTimeout`
A manual `controller.abort(reason)` with a custom reason still makes the awaited fetch throw an `AbortError` DOMException rather than that reason value; DOMException carries no legacy numeric `.code`
notes: `fetch(url, { signal })` cancellation works — pre-flight, mid-flight, and via **`AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`**, on both the top-level `await` path and the fiber path (a fetch awaited inside an `http.listen` handler): the await loop checks the signal every spin, and the event loop folds the timeout deadline into its `select()` wait so an idle loop wakes at the deadline — then tears the transfer down and throws a **`DOMException`** (`instanceof DOMException` and, since it inherits `Error`, `instanceof Error` both hold), named `AbortError` for a manual abort and `TimeoutError` for a timeout ([ADR-00237](../adr/ADR-00237.md)–[ADR-00240](../adr/ADR-00240.md))

`new DOMException(message?, name?)` is constructible directly; `AbortSignal` is an object with `aborted`/`reason`/`deadlineNs` plus a hidden listener map — an EventTarget that fires `"abort"`; its pointer rides on the fetch's pending handle, and `__kml_signal_aborted` folds the timeout deadline in for the await loop, the event-loop resume scan, and the `select()` wait ([TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00236](../adr/ADR-00236.md)–[ADR-00240](../adr/ADR-00240.md))
